solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glass fitter's no good, being less inclined to work

indicators.note: 'no good' tells us the letter for good is dropped from the glass fitter

parts.note: a glazier is a tradesman who fits glass in windows

explanation.surface: A tradesman's poor workmanship is put down to his idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazier is the comparative of lazy, describing someone with less appetite for effort or work.

clue.text: With a couple of pints almost top up water tanks

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a quart is two pints

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: A1 means top-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Fill up the fish tanks with nearly two pints.
explanation.walkthrough: QUART loses its T, and AI (A1) read upwards gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria is the plural of aquarium, a glass tank for keeping fish and other water life.

clue.text: Native of South America imprisoned?

parts.note: imprisoned means in the can, can being slang for prison
can is slang for a jail, as in 'in the can'

explanation.surface: An indigenous Andean person has been locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: One word gives two pieces: 'in the can' is slang for being in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An Incan is a member of the Inca people, whose empire spread along the Andes of South America.

clue.text: Give extra support to sappers in army unit

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army corps whose soldiers are called sappers
a force is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Engineers are sent to bolster a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen by adding extra people, material or support.

clue.text: Crossing town in France, bounder made petty comments

indicators.note: the bounder stretches across the French town, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: a cad is an old-fashioned word for a bounder, a dishonourable man
ville is the French word for town

explanation.surface: A rogue travelling through a French town grumbles about trifles.
explanation.walkthrough: The cad's letters go around VILLE, giving CA-VILLE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise trivial objections, so the past tense matches making petty comments.

clue.text: Rampant deflation in City? That's something you may never know

indicators.note: rampant suggests letters running wild, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: Runaway falling prices in the financial district may be kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Confidentiality is secrecy: what is kept confidential is withheld from outsiders, who may never learn it.

clue.text: More than one climber struggles to cross Matterhorn ultimately

indicators.note: the struggling word crosses over the letter, so it sits within

parts.note: vies means competes or struggles

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the mountain's name

explanation.surface: A mountaineer struggles to get across the Matterhorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer, but the definition means climbing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants like ivy or grapevines are climbers, so the plural word means several such plants.

clue.text: See there's a problem and be discouraged

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: problem tells us the letters of the words beside it are in disarray

explanation.surface: Seeing there is trouble ahead, one gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb of understanding, but it is the old exclamation; 'problem' signals that the letters of 'there's a' are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom meaning to become dispirited and stop trying.

clue.text: Formerly buxom model

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
ample describes a full, plump figure

explanation.surface: A one-time curvy fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a fashion model, but it means a pattern to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a model to be imitated or a typical instance of something.

clue.text: Judge wanting harmony about court meeting

indicators.note: the word for harmony is placed about the court abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: union means harmony or concord

explanation.surface: A judge longs for peace before a court session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is only a link here, not a deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction is a point where roads or lines come together, a place of meeting.

clue.text: Steamy saunas somewhere in the Bahamas

indicators.note: steamy suggests the letters of the saunas are heated up and jumbled

explanation.surface: Hot sweating rooms are a feature of a Caribbean resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas, located on New Providence island.

clue.text: Insects from various parts of France — whoppers

indicators.note: the parts of the country's name come in various orders, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: whoppers are big lies

explanation.surface: Tall stories told about insects found in assorted French regions.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging FRANCE gives CRANEF, then LIES is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Crane flies, or daddy-long-legs, are long-legged insects of the family Tipulidae.

clue.text: Smooth operator harbours feeling of confidence

indicators.note: the two words harbour the answer, holding it across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A slick charmer hides a sense of self-belief.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the last of 'Smooth' into the start of 'operator'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is an expectant trust that something wished for will come about.

clue.text: Talk about American Great Lake

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
US stands for American, as in United States
Erie is one of North America's five Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A discussion concerning one of the Great Lakes of the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk about' looks like one phrase, but 'about' gives CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A causerie is an informal chat or a light conversational essay, from French.

clue.text: Bargain hunter reflected stainless kitchenware will save very little money

indicators.note: the reversed words keep the money safe within them
reflected means the words are read backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: pure means unsullied or stainless
pans are kitchen utensils
p, a penny, is a tiny sum

explanation.surface: Shiny steel pots in a mirror, bought cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns both words together, and 'will save' then holds the penny inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper-up is someone who grabs opportunities quickly, like a shopper seizing bargains.

clue.text: Actor's introduction to porn film

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link; the definition is the actor

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, as of oil on water

explanation.surface: A performer's first step into adult cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage, in the old sense of a member of a theatre company.

clue.text: Supporting strike action, choose, say, to collect money

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: the example abbreviation collects the money, taking it inside

parts.note: e.g. stands for 'for example', which say also means
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Striking workers decide to gather donations.
explanation.definitionFit: Picketing is standing outside a workplace to support a strike and discourage others from entering.

clue.text: Out of shape

parts.note: read as 'one out of the shapes', a geometric figure; also 'out' as unfashionable

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means unfit, but it reads as 'one from the set of shapes', and an unfashionable person is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A square is a basic geometric figure, and in slang a square is someone hopelessly unfashionable.

clue.text: A fraction of compassion?

definitions.meaning: mercy shown to a defeated enemy

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a fourth part of something and mercy granted to a beaten opponent.

clue.text: After trance, oddly I become very quiet

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word trance

parts.note: to turn means to become, as milk turns sour

explanation.surface: Someone falls silent after being in a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a link; the pieces are taken in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn describes a person who habitually says very little, reserved in speech.

clue.text: Upset, finding females were in control all round

indicators.note: the ruling word goes all round the females

parts.note: ruled means held power or were in control
F is the abbreviation for female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Annoyed to find women were in charge everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled means flustered or upset, as feathers are disturbed.

clue.text: American citizen made little noise, presumably

definitions.meaning: a White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, an American of the old establishment
read as 'was p', p being the musical mark for soft or quiet

explanation.walkthrough: In music p (piano) means quiet, so 'was p' means was quiet: the second definition splits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names a privileged white Protestant American; split in two it says 'was quiet'.

clue.text: Express and Financial Times containing article on Conservative leader's latest show of political skill

indicators.note: the two newspaper-like words hold the remaining pieces between them

parts.note: to state is to express
FT is the familiar short name of the Financial Times newspaper

indicators.note: in an across clue, the article placed on the others follows them
the latest letter of a word is its final one

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Two British newspapers carry an item on the Tory leader's latest display of political skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express and the Financial Times are both British national newspapers; 'Express' here is a verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the art of conducting government affairs, a skill shown in political leadership.

clue.text: One way of contacting people that's a bit risky perhaps

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase gives the answer, which lies across its words

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with people this way may be slightly dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is part of the text: the letters run across riSKY PErhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Skype is an internet service for video and voice calls, a way to contact people.

clue.text: Study English writer

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A student studies an English author.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English novelist and dramatist.

clue.text: Passionate tale about maiden

indicators.note: the tale goes about the maiden, enclosing her letter

parts.note: a story is a tale
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A romantic story of a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy can describe a relationship or temperament full of strong, turbulent emotion.

clue.text: One swallowing drug during race is likely to be followed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the race swallows the drug, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a mile is a classic distance for a race
a tab is a tablet, slang for a dose of a drug

explanation.surface: An athlete is caught taking drugs mid-race, setting a bad example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' only reinforces 'swallowing': the drug ends up inside the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imitable can be copied, so it is likely to be followed as a model.

clue.text: Infamous Victorian wearing extremely flashy showy trinkets

indicators.note: the Victorian wears the outer letters, which go around him
extremely picks the two extreme letters of the word

parts.note: Jack the Ripper was the notorious murderer of Victorian London

explanation.surface: A notorious Victorian villain decked out in flamboyant baubles.
explanation.walkthrough: F and Y, the ends of 'flashy', surround RIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Frippery means showy, trivial ornament: frills and trinkets of little value.

clue.text: Gluttonous journalist tucked into a sort of mullet

indicators.note: the journalist goes inside the fish's name, tucked into it

parts.note: the grey mullet is a common type of fish
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A greedy reporter tucks into a plate of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but it is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy and gluttonous are synonyms, both meaning eager to eat more than one needs.
